files_summary.users.json:
JSON array of 10 user objects. Each object contains:
- user_id (e.g., "U0001")
- username (e.g., "user1")
- email (e.g., "user1@example.com")
- entity (always "example-team")
- created_at (ISO‑8601 timestamp).
files_summary.projects.json:
JSON array of 5 project objects for the entity "example-team". Each object includes:
- name (project slug, e.g., "image-classification")
- entity
- description
- visibility ("public" or "private")
- created_at / updated_at (ISO timestamps)
- tags (list of 3 descriptive tags).
files_summary.runs.csv:
CSV file with 100 synthetic run records (plus header). Columns:
- run_id (8‑character alphanumeric ID)
- project_name (one of the 5 projects)
- display_name (human‑readable name, e.g., "image-classification_run_3")
- state ("finished", "running" or "failed")
- created_at (ISO timestamp)
- accuracy (float, 0.6‑0.99)
- loss (float, 0.1‑2.0)
- learning_rate (float, e.g., 0.0001)
- batch_size (16/32/64/128)
- epochs (5/10/20/50)
- user_id (links to a user in users.json).
files_summary.artifacts.json:
JSON array of 50 artifact entries (10 per project). Each artifact includes:
- artifact_id (unique ID)
- project_name
- name (e.g., "image-classification_artifact_7")
- version (e.g., "v3")
- digest (UUID hex string)
- size_bytes (1 MiB – 1 GiB)
- created_at (ISO timestamp)
- metadata object with fields:
  • framework ("torch", "tensorflow" or "jax")
  • model_type (e.g., "resnet", "bert", "gpt", "dqn", "vae")
  • description (text describing the artifact).
files_summary.traces.json:
JSON array of 227 Weave trace objects (roots + children). Each trace record contains:
- id (unique sequential ID like "T000001")
- trace_id (UUID shared among related traces)
- parent_id (null for root traces; otherwise points to the parent trace id)
- project_name (one of the 5 projects)
- op_name (URI style string, e.g., "weave:///root_op_4")
- display_name (readable label)
- started_at / ended_at (ISO timestamps)
- status ("success" or "error")
- latency_ms (integer)
- costs object with:
  • prompt_tokens_total_cost (float)
  • completion_tokens_total_cost (float)
  • total_cost (sum of the two)
- attributes object with:
  • model_name (e.g., "gpt-4")
  • token_count (integer).
The traces reflect a realistic parent‑child hierarchy (15 root traces per project, each with 1‑3 child traces).
files_summary.README.md: Schema, lifecycles and business rules of this benchmark's datastore.

tool_schemas.name: list_users
tool_schemas.description: Lists users, optionally filtered by identifiers, exact fields (username/email/entity), creation time window, or a free-text query, and can paginate/sort the results; it returns the matching user objects and, when requested, a total count. It refuses requests that provide unknown parameters, unsupported sort fields or sort directions, or invalid pagination inputs (for example a non-integer limit or a cursor it can’t interpret). It also refuses invalid timestamps for created_after/created_before and rejects filter combinations it cannot apply consistently (such as an invalid user_id format).

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for pagination to fetch the next page of results.

user_id.description: Filter to a specific user identifier, e.g., "U0001".

email.description: Filter users by exact email address.

created_after.description: Include users created at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

created_before.description: Include users created at or before this timestamp (ISO 8601).

q.description: Free-text search over common user fields (e.g., username/email).

include_total.description: Whether to include the total count of matching users (may be slower).

tool_schemas.name: get_user
tool_schemas.description: Fetches and returns the single user object identified by user_id. It refuses requests missing user_id or with a malformed user_id value. It also refuses the request when no user exists for the given identifier.

user_id.description: The identifier of the user, e.g., "U0001".

tool_schemas.name: list_projects
tool_schemas.description: Lists projects, with optional filtering by project slug, owning entity, visibility, tag, created/updated time windows, and free-text search, and supports pagination and sorting; it returns the matching project objects and, when requested, a total count. It refuses requests that include unknown parameters, invalid sort_by/sort_order values, or pagination inputs it cannot validate (such as a non-integer limit or an unreadable cursor). It also refuses invalid ISO 8601 timestamps for created_*/updated_* filters and rejects visibility or project_name values outside the supported set.

limit.description: Maximum number of projects to return.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for pagination to fetch the next page of results.

project_name.description: Filter to a specific project slug/name.

tag.description: Filter projects that contain this tag.

created_after.description: Include projects created at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

created_before.description: Include projects created at or before this timestamp (ISO 8601).

updated_after.description: Include projects updated at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

updated_before.description: Include projects updated at or before this timestamp (ISO 8601).

q.description: Free-text search over common project fields (e.g., name/description).

include_total.description: Whether to include the total count of matching projects (may be slower).

tool_schemas.name: get_project
tool_schemas.description: Fetches and returns the single project identified by project_name. It refuses requests missing project_name or with a project_name value outside the supported slugs. It also refuses the request when no project matches the given name.

project_name.description: The slug/name of the project, e.g., "image-classification".

tool_schemas.name: list_runs
tool_schemas.description: Lists run records and returns the runs that match the provided filters such as project_name, state, user_id, metric thresholds (accuracy/loss), and training settings (batch_size/epochs). It refuses requests with unknown parameters or filters of the wrong type (for example non-numeric min/max values or non-integer batch_size/epochs). It also refuses conflicting ranges (such as min_accuracy greater than max_accuracy or min_loss greater than max_loss) and rejects filters that reference entities that don’t exist or can’t be resolved (such as an unknown project_name or user_id).

project_name.description: Filter runs belonging to a specific project.

user_id.description: Filter by the user who launched the run.

min_accuracy.description: Include runs with accuracy greater than or equal to this value.

max_accuracy.description: Include runs with accuracy less than or equal to this value.

min_loss.description: Include runs with loss greater than or equal to this value.

max_loss.description: Include runs with loss less than or equal to this value.

batch_size.description: Filter runs that used a specific batch size.

epochs.description: Filter runs that were trained for a specific number of epochs.

tool_schemas.name: get_run
tool_schemas.description: Fetches and returns the single run record identified by run_id. It refuses requests missing run_id or where run_id is not an 8-character alphanumeric identifier. It also refuses the request when no run exists with that ID.

run_id.description: The 8‑character alphanumeric ID of the run.

tool_schemas.name: list_artifacts
tool_schemas.description: Lists artifact entries and returns the artifacts that match the optional filters for project_name, framework, and model_type. It refuses requests with unknown parameters or a framework value outside the supported set. It also refuses filters that reference a project that doesn’t exist or can’t be resolved.

project_name.description: Filter artifacts belonging to a specific project.

framework.description: Filter by the ML framework used.

tool_schemas.name: get_artifact
tool_schemas.description: Fetches and returns the single artifact entry identified by artifact_id. It refuses requests missing artifact_id or with an artifact_id value it cannot validate. It also refuses the request when no artifact exists for the given identifier.

artifact_id.description: The unique identifier of the artifact.

tool_schemas.name: list_traces
tool_schemas.description: Lists trace records and returns traces matching the optional filters for project_name, status, parent_id, and an op_name substring. It refuses requests with unknown parameters, a status value outside the supported set, or filter values it cannot interpret (such as an invalid parent_id). It also refuses requests that reference a project that doesn’t exist or can’t be resolved.

project_name.description: Filter traces belonging to a specific project.

parent_id.description: Return only child traces of the given parent trace ID.

op_name_contains.description: Return traces whose `op_name` contains this substring.

tool_schemas.name: get_trace
tool_schemas.description: Fetches and returns the single trace record identified by trace_id. It refuses requests missing trace_id or with a trace_id that is not a valid UUID. It also refuses the request when no trace exists for the given identifier.

trace_id.description: The UUID identifying the trace (shared among related spans).

metadata.name: SageTrail ML Workspace
metadata.description: A lightweight backend for browsing machine learning projects, users, runs, artifacts, and execution traces via simple listing and retrieval APIs.
